comment: She is an incredibly kind-hearted woman. She's very compassionate and sympathizes with the struggles of being a student. She's even better one-on-one. Super helpful!

title: Professor in the Biology department at Frostburg State University
comment: <TEACHER> is by far one of the greatest professors I've ever had. Gives weekly quizzes with super clear study guides so there's no reason to get anything less than 100%. The tests aren't easy, but they aren't hard either. Just show up to class and do the study guide and you should be fine. Plus his lectures are awesome! He's easy on the eyes too

title: Professor in the Biology department at Frostburg State University
comment: <TEACHER> overall makes this class easy to pass and very informational for a student not majoring in Biology. The information you learn is useful, and he keeps it very interesting. Make sure to take advantage of quiz materials.

title: Professor in the Biology department at Frostburg State University
comment: Easiest class I have ever taken. I got an email at the end of the semester saying that I had the highest grade out of 190 students across all Bio 109 classes, even though I never studied, never took notes, and never reviewed powerpoints outside of class. Class is optional but if you go then you wont need to do anything outside of class to get an A.

title: Professor in the Biology department at Frostburg State University
comment: <TEACHER> is a very nice guy. Weekly quizzes and three exams. You have to study really hard for the exams or you will have no chance of passing them. His exams are extremely difficult because he has trick questions and long complex questions. He has group work in class to help buffer your grade. Attendance isn't mandatory.

title: Professor in the Nursing department at State College of Florida Manatee-Sarasota
comment: All the BSN classes are basically the same design but with different topics, and all follow the same grading rubics.  On discussion posts he is very "nit-picky" on grading, and gives grades significantly less than the 6 other professors i've had, despite using the same department wide grading rubic.

title: Professor in the Environment department at SUNY Potsdam
comment: <TEACHER> is a wonderful human and teacher. If you're a therapeutic recreation or wilderness ed minor, you'll get to have him as an advisor as well as a teacher! He really cares about each of his students as people and will take the time to get to know you. Sometimes his Moodle site can be confusing, but he's awesome anyway.

title: Professor in the Environment department at SUNY Potsdam
comment: <TEACHER> <TEACHER> is the greatest Professor to grace SUNY Potsdam. He is an inspirational leader who works towards the better wellbeing of Wilderness Education and his students. His classes are challenging but in the right ways, if you study, participate and work hard you will receive the grade you deserve. <TEACHER> is easy to work with and a big motivator!

title: Professor in the Environment department at SUNY Potsdam
comment: <TEACHER> started off my first class with him with a fifteen-minute joke about cheese that didn't have a punchline, if that gives any indication as to what kind of teacher he is.

title: Professor in the Environment department at SUNY Potsdam
comment: <TEACHER> is such a nice guy! Took his speech class and he made me feel like I was in a very comfortable atmosphere for giving my speeches. He is very funny and sarcastic and just generally a great professor to have!

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Tri-County Technical College
comment: <TEACHER> <TEACHER> is an extremely helpful professor. He wants to see his students thrive and pass!

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Victor Valley College
comment: I could not understand the material and he did not explain it well.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Victor Valley College
comment: <TEACHER> is an all round nice guy .lectures are confusing because he lives far from  the school it seems like he rushes through chapters to finish them instead of really teaching. If you have questions he isn't always clear on what the answer actually is or if you're wrong or not . final is 25% of your entire grade.  Relies fast to emails.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Victor Valley College
comment: Homework is online, but work is turned in as if it wasn't done online; lectures are informative, but VERY dry; not too interactive with the class; I've caught some errors in his grading, especially when the first test total was miscalculated for everyone's

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Victor Valley College
comment: not enough work problems to practice. all test are on in class. if you did not study you will not pass. will review the test with you.  online work is not organized. homework yes. no extra credit.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Victor Valley College
comment: <TEACHER> is not the most organised person. He works at 2 other collegeshigh schools, so he is pretty much always busy. He has a thick accent, but is usually pretty easy to understand. the real problem, is that his whole class is failing, and he doesn't do anything to help. We go over a lecture that he didn't write in class. Bad experience for math.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: She is a very caring professor and wants to know that you are doing well outside of class. It is hard to understand her sometimes, but that is because English is her second language. Besides that, I enjoyed having her as a professor.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: Best professor I could have asked for! She gives us a lot of practice in class with the material to help learn it and has a visual teaching style. She cares about her students and does her best to make the course engaging. As long as you participate you will do great. Overall one of the best Spanish professors I have had!

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: Incredible professor. The class is taught almost fully in Spanish but in a way that is easy for non-fluent speakers to understand. She is very kind and can be fun, and her feedback on our essays and tests was always very helpful. And there're many chances to bring up your grade with revisions and homework.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: <TEACHER> is the best! Shes so kind and sweet, and a really great spanish teacher. If you're hesitant about spanish, take it with <TEACHER>! I have taken spanish for years and have never understood it so well. She is very fun and genuinely cares for her students. I was definitely scared to take a 300 level spanish class, but she makes it easy

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: <TEACHER> is a solid choice for a SPAN 200 professor. She cant do much to make the class more interesting, as its a very baseline class at CNU, but she makes it as easy as it can be. Shes a very nice person and always wants to help her students. Very nice grader and overall a fun class. I recommend her!

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: Not impressed, she is a native speaker which is a Plus but other then that would not take her again.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: <TEACHER> was very willing to meet outside of class to help students. There were a considerable amount of writing assignments but they weren't too long and were definitely manageable. The digital components of this class like using twitter and memes to learn/ practice Spanish were a nice break from normal lectures. I would take this class again!

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: I took International Cinema with <TEACHER> and I would never do it again. She is a nice woman, but very annoying at times and VERY opinionated. If you can get another professor for this course, do it. She's not terrible, but sometimes hard to tolerate. There are a lot of quizzes also.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at Christopher Newport University
comment: <TEACHER> is nice! She doesn't assign much written homework, although we did a lot of WebSAM online homework. The tests have a weird "culture" part on them, but she thinks it's unfair and said that next semester might be different. She's helpful when you need it! If you've already taken three years of high school Spanish, you'll be fine in 200.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Medgar Evers College
comment: Took this class during the summer, and she is a pretty fair grader. Basically you earn your grade. If you don't do the work she will not feel bad to fail you. Great at explaining, expects you to be in class on time, test were based on HW, try not to miss class, participation is important, she like good work ethics, and showing interest in ur grade.

title: Professor in the Aeronautics department at Saint Louis University
comment: Very good teacher and class. She makes the material interesting and clear to understand, however, she grades very harshly on tests so you have to be extremely specific and detailed about everything. She does go over the tests with you afterwards and is always available to talk. Be prepared for a long but easy paper, which she also reviews for you.

title: Professor in the Marketing department at Berkeley College
comment: She is AWESOME. I learned so MUCH in her class. She is not easy at all, and really pushes you to work for your grade. She has a lovely personality, and is helpful. Just be sure not to send her e-mail. It would better to speak with her after or during class.  She is one of my favorite professors at Berkeley.  You won't regret having her for a prof'.

title: Professor in the Marketing department at Berkeley College
comment: Best teacher ever. She's structured and clear, and make sure you're always prepared for your classes. Gives quizzes and homework almost every class, but not difficult ones. Just to keep you on track. She is hilarious, cool and energetic! Great lectures.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Manhattan Community College
comment: <TEACHER> really is a lovely person who obviously has a passion for and clear understanding of mathematics. Unfortunately that really doesn't translate to her teaching.  Get ready to study a ton, get knocked down points for nit-picky things, and still struggle on tests in spite of understanding the concepts. Incredibly frustrating.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: I thought this class was going to be extremely hard and the first few weeks, it seems intimidating. All you really need to do is fill out his study guides, and it is basically the exam. No attendance, but throws in a pop quiz here and there. I never paid attention and just studied the study guide and got an A on every exam. He's a really nice guy.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Great Econ Professor.  I really enjoyed his class.  You really have to study, and adjust your learning style.  Read the textbook.  I am a visual learner, so I went through the textbook & watched videos on each subject after lecture.  I would re-watch the videos before class.  If given a study guide I would watch videos on each topic if needed.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Had him for microeconomics. He is really smart and definitely knows his stuff.  The textbook is dry and sometimes lectures but he tells jokes and had some practice problems reference Pokemon go and other popular culture to keep it interesting, but let's face it, economics is not exactly exciting any way you slice it.  Very helpful in office hours.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: LOTS of writing and work, although writing is not an issue for me so I did well on those assignments. LOTS of extra credit opportunity. I was sure I failed 3/4 quizzes, but ended up getting above a 96% on ALL of them (generous quiz grader). Make friends who attend class if you hate long lectures so that you don't miss the "surprise" quizzes.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: HEAVY coursework. This class was awful, he goes into too much detail than what you need to know for a 101 class,and I don't know why it is not a writing intensive class, because IT IS. 2 exams(midterm/final), two 3-page papers on the books you read,one 2-page report,TEN 1-page globalization journals,and 4-10 surprise quizzes. So you HAVE to attend.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Had him last semester for senior year. It was a lot of work for a 101 class, but I took a lot from the class. Learned about exchange rates , assets, and profits. I'm non business major but it helped me with interviewing at the clinic I work at now.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: He's very hard to understand if you're just taking this as a requirement and have no interest in economics. He is also the slowest grader ever. You will never know your grade until after finals.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Goes more in depth than the book. Problems and calculations  for car loans, retirement, etc. Insurance was boring but otherwise made finance fun to watch.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: I am a finance major and took this as an elective. He is VERY knowledgeabl in what he talks about but the delivery is bad. The course was long. In class examples weren't the best. He expected you to know financial functions on excel. 10 one page papers due by the end of the semester. Test were easy if you studied the study guide.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: <TEACHER> is an awesome teacher but does makes things challenging. He knows his stuff and goes into greater depth than the book on a lot of topics

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Prof. <TEACHER> is knowledgeable about business, but pretty funny too. One time made a joke with that Trainor bass song to teach about base currency for exchange rates. He does cover quite a bit for a 101 class. He goes over financial statements which can be intense if you are new to it, but he lets you pick the company you want for the paper.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: I learned more about exchange rates and companies. Always helps and explains more if you ask questions after class.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: Great teacher. Pretty new, but younger and can relate to him more. Course is pretty easy, just come to class and stay up to date and you'll do just fine.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: <TEACHER> is the man. He's very helpful and class is not bad at all if you attend. That's basically how all college classes are, attend and you'll usually do decent. I recommend him and some of his higher level business classes as well if you're really interested in finance.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: <TEACHER> is extremely knowledgeable in international business. The class wasn't easy, and that's why I took so much out of the course.    His  short cartoons and pop-culture references are refreshing, but make sure to pay attention and study for his tests.  If you're dedicated to your studies and smart, you'll do well and learn something.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: I liked the class, Prof. <TEACHER> tries to make examples fun with a short cartoon as a gag, to get you interested. Other stuff was cool to learn like exchange rates affecting how much stuff you can buy when you travel.

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University
comment: flexible on due dates, you have to show up in case of a quiz, heavier workload than one might think

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University

title: Professor in the Business department at Benedictine University

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: I don't think I have ever had such a dense professor that doesn't acknowledge that online school has changed our education system entirely. Her teaching methods are antiquated and boring. She made us write a cover letter and resume as part of our final which is classist and contributes to the perpetuated belief that our value as humans is working

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH DR. TROTTER! She is not a good professor. This is a great class if you want to learn about how her sons are doing or how hard she had it growing up. The only thing I learned from this class was how to spell psychology...

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: Online class. Clear on what was expected and how she grades. NO makeups. The Wiley assignments are all critical thinking, so you must make sure you understand fully what you are reading. She was always quick to respond to emails and the discussion boards. I would take her for another online class.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: There is a lot of material to read, but the orion assignments and tests are fairly easy. She cares about the students and encourages them to talk and share information.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

I just wouldn't take her she is a good teacher and knows her stuff but she cant stay on topic long enough for you to learn it.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: This professor goes on tangents that do not pertain to the class, she doesn't really teach. Would not recommend her EVER!

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: Horrible! Would not recommend! Class consist of ALL ORION assignments that are specifically due at 5:00pm and often are not available until the day before due.  No additional handouts. Must fer-batum read the book and sit through hours of Orion.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: I absolutely hated this class. I'm not the lazy student and tried my best on ever test and passed with a B or higher. Her handouts are only worth 5 points. title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: I thought it was a great class. Orion the online program was a great help. It made sure you really knew the material. Easy A!

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville

Everything that is covered in class and in the book is on the quiz and test. she relates everything back to real word situations, and got to know her students. <TEACHER> is the best!

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: Not a good professor.  She's not overly difficult if you NEED the class but if you can find another teacher then you're probably better off.  She often presents "facts" in biased ways and often ses closed minded although she'd tell you otherwise.  The amount of work was a lot.  Not an easy A.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: Doesn't care about you or your grade. My class didn't say it was a Hybrid but it is. You use an online program called Orion. Stupid and a waste of time. Would not take again or recommend to anyone.

title: Professor in the Psychology department at Florida State College at Jacksonville
comment: Lectures don't help much with what is going to be on the test. Only way I got a B is by doing the journals and interview paper.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: *NOT ENG361, I had her in ENG434. She's incredible, by far my favorite professor at A&M. Lectures are always engaging and mainly discussion based. Attendance mandatory, but she'll work with you. Reading responses before every class. Super caring and passionate about everything she teaches. If you only take one English class at A&M, make it hers!

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: <TEACHER> is definitely a kind, knowledgeable individual and is definitely an expert in her field. That being said, I will never take another class of hers. Discussions are one-sided and tend to vilify women. She makes it known EVERY CLASS that she is not a feminist. That on top of loads of homework and awful grading rubrics = never again.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: TOUGH grader. I have never received such low grades on papers before. Very nice and passionate professor but grades extremely hard and requires attendance. 3 discussion boards weekly, several papers, and an 8-10 page final paper. Reads 7+ books throughout the semester with in-class & online discussion. Didn't expect to get a C in an elective class

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: LOVE <TEACHER>! Absolutely amazing, clearly passionate. Lectures are always fun, more discussion-based. Tons of reading and almost daily reading responses, so be ready. Highly recommend this class, <TEACHER> is incredible and super understanding if you need an extension or anything. One of my favorite classes of all time :)

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: I love <TEACHER>! The class was amazing! I enjoyed reading different types of books each week. I will say if you are not an avid reader, this class can be a lot. Coming to class allowed me to verbalize my thoughts on the book in a group setting. I only received a C is because the first test was difficult. Wonderful class and Professor!

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: This class is not an easy A. I have done all the assignments and have a C. The midterm was insanely hard. Prof put a 7 point curve due to the amount of Fs. Has a 8-10 page paper that is 30% of grade. The prof is nice, but is hard.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: The most passionate professor I have EVER met. Took 331 and 343. Lectures are discussion based w/ student involvement. Have to read + a writing assignment before every class. One semi-hard midterm, one optional final. One 10+ page final paper, but you spend months writing it and she guides you a lot. B if you do all the work, A w/ extra effort

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: I took this course with <TEACHER> because all the reviews of her were really good and it seemed like an easy A. That was not the case at all. She picks favorites and grades accordingly. Evidently, I was not one of her favorites and my grade suffered from this. She grades extremely tough and provides little to no feedback.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: This class should be labeled as writing and reading intensive. Two LENGTHY discussion posts a week that involves so much reading and a 10-page research paper. The amount of work in this class is ridiculous. <TEACHER> is very passionate about what she teaches and is extremely nice and thoughtful, but the amount of work ruins that.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: Such a sweet woman and it's very clear she's passionate about what she teaches! However there is SO MUCH reading for this class it's insane. There's a midterm, discussion posts, group project, essay, and an optional final.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: <TEACHER> is a nice professor who has good knowledge in literature but she gives A LOT of homework and readings. The exams are half matching and half short answer which is also tough. She's very helpful and all but for the sake of my academics I wouldnt take her again.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: I'm a science person so to be fair LIT is not my area but this class was SO MUCH work and too much reading. Her exam is short answer which is unfortunate. She doesn't give you much to go off of with how to study.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: Absolutely loved Prof. <TEACHER>. You can tell she's passionate and knowledgeable about the literature. Classes are discussion-based and a lot of fun if you did the reading. We would often have to read entire 300-page books in one week. If you stay ahead of it it shouldn't be too difficult. Probably the only prof I'm going to miss once class ends.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: I know what you're thinking: "Children's lit, how hard can that be?" That's exactly what I thought when registering for classes, BUT this class is way too involved. You will read a new book each week and write a response for it before each class. Each response takes me an hour. Take another ENGL class, don't put yourself through this one.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: BE WARNED- You will have a reading response due before every class! These take at least 45 minutes to complete. I am a senior, I've taken 3 writing intensive courses and have NEVER had to do so much homework/writing for a class. <TEACHER> is very nice but I wish I would've known how much work it was before registering for this class.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: <TEACHER> is the best human I've ever met in my life. Her class is extremely interesting but I wouldn't recommend taking more english classes alongside hers as the workload is quite heavy. It's very worth it, but it's very easy to fall behind. There is a reading response due every class, but if you keep up, you're golden.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: She's a lot of fun in class and makes you really interested in the subject matter, but on tests and papers she grades really harshly and it's hard to get feedback about why you lost points.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: <TEACHER> is a great teacher who is passionate about what she is teaching . She is willing to help her students and give them feedback so that they may succeed in her class. However, she is one of the harder English teachers I have ever taken. The assignments themselves were not difficult, but were very time consuming and often tedious.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: <TEACHER> is passionate, engaging, and incredibly knowledable! The class itself was a significant amount of reading, with discussions due each class. One midterm, essay, and an optional final. The current TA has made this class very difficult to get an A in and she clearly has differing opinions than <TEACHER> when it comes to grading.

title: Professor in the English department at Texas A&M University at College Station
comment: The professor herself is really sweet and cares about her students opinions and if they learn or not. We've had over 14 books this semester to read and a discussion post due before every class. Honestly I never touched a single book and just googled the stuff for the discussions or got ideas from other students posts. Our TA was terrible!!

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Super nice and easy to work with. She expects a lot from you but this is college. If you meet with her before the paper deadline, or even email her your paper, she will give very helpful feedback on what to fix so that you are almost guaranteed a good grade. I sent her my paper several times and she was always enthusiastic to help. Loved her class.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: She was super caring, she expects a lot but she helps you get there.  She met with me several times outside of class to help me clean up my papers.  Highly recommend her.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Sam explains assignments well and tells you what she wants on assignments. Gives great feedback. She is dorky and hilarious. Use her office hours to get more feedback on papers and make sure you go to class. Also, expect a normal amount of writing from any ENG 101 class. Only complaint is that we didn't need two of our textbooks.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Sam is an amazing teacher!! The best one I had yet at CMU. She doesn't talk down to you and is such an easy grader. If you turn on your assignments she will see that and give you a good grade. Super nice and works with your schedule to meet with you and help with anything. I highly suggest taking her class, you won't regret it.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Favorite professor so far at CMU. Really wants you to succeed and puts in the effort to help you. Go to conferences about essays, they really help. She's the best for ENG1o1. Expect a lot of writing but it doesn't seem like busy work. Take her if you can

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Sam is a wonderful professor. She really helps you improve especially on the essays. Don't be afraid to conference with her and ask her for help. Take ENG101 with her, she is funny and does sweet activities.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: Very tough grader. Doing what the assignment asks is "C" work. Have to work VERY hard for anything above a C. Expects different quality work from different students which makes grading even worse.

title: Professor in the English department at Central Michigan University
comment: If you do everything right on a paper you will get a C. She also will take points off a paper if she sees you with your phone, catch is she wont tell you that she sees you. She's a nice person but she treats us like children. She also gave exams every Friday that a big weekend came up, meaning you can't skip to head out early. Even Spring Break.

title: Professor in the Information Technology department at College of Southern Idaho
comment: You only have projects to do, the online textbook is very helpful. He is very good at giving you feedback and wants to help you.

title: Professor in the Information Technology department at College of Southern Idaho
comment: Lots to do in class but a great professor.

title: Professor in the Information Technology department at College of Southern Idaho

title: Professor in the Philosophy department at St. Petersburg College (all campuses)
comment: <TEACHER> is a wonderful professor when beginning in philosophy. He gradually increases the difficulty of the material throughout the semester but never too much that it's unmanageable. There's a weekly quiz and 4 papers including the final paper, no tests. He is easy to reach outside of class and very understanding, definitely recommend!

title: Professor in the Philosophy department at St. Petersburg College (all campuses)
comment: Honors Cornerstone is a combined philosophy analysis skills/life goal setting class that's mandatory for the Honors Program. You'll work from notes and PPTs. Top students with genius IQ's. You'll walk out with clearer goals, new key life/academic survival skills, support team, life reading list. Possibly the most valuable, practical  class to take.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is a good mathematician and teacher. I thought he was neither too tough nor too easy. He follows his syllabus schedule strictly, but he makes sure that the most important ideas are presented upfront clearly and thoroughly.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: I make it a point to try and take him every semester. He's a brilliant man and an excellent teacher. Keep in mind that he is a mathematician, and will do his best to ensure that you really understand the math. If you want to get by doing the plug and chug, he will mop the floor with you on exam day. Ask him for help, learn the math and get an A.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> often relies on the class to answer him to move on, so if you are uncomfortable with participation and shouting out answers maybe not the best teacher for your style of learning. Teaches math via definitions and examples on the white board, essentially walking you through problems every class. I would take math class with him again.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> got annoyed when the class did not ask questions or when we had forgotten material from Calc 1 or when we were nervous laughing at the seemingly insurmountable equations. Typical lecture style. Not an engaging professor.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: He really shows his best for the lectures that he does. He makes sure every student of his does their best and will help when it is needed.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is by far one of my favorite professors here at NAU! He is funny and makes the class fun. I had a rough time at the beginning of the semester and he worked with me so I wouldn't fail the class because of it. Calc 2 is a tough subject but I think <TEACHER> makes it easier to understand.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is an amazing professor--one of the best I've had. He is very respected in the math department and among the students. He is always in his office and is always there to help you. Every lecture he gives a mini quiz (1 question that takes >5 mins) that is meant to improve your grade. He tries his hardest to make the course as easy as possible.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: Probably one of the best math professors I had. If you take the time to learn the material and ask question at office hours, you will do fine. Go to the test review sessions, they help a lot! He explains material well and the exams are not hard if you study.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: You're expected to do proof presentations a few times throughout the semester. If you're proofing ability isn't good, then you're going to have a very difficult time.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is a great teacher! Each week, there's one paper homework and 3-5 short online assignments. Always willing to help in his office or during class hours. Spends time at the beginning of class taking questions from homework. If you study for the tests, they are fine and pretty easy; if you don't, expect to fail. Textbook is just a workbook for HW

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is a good teacher. He is a little unorganized  but gives a lot of examples in class and does proofs to show how/ why certain formulas work. There was usually one paper homework and 3-5 webworks due a week. <TEACHER> was always willing to go over any homework question in class. Test were not to hard but not that easy gives lots of partial credit

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: He's a good guy and you can tell he's really into numerical analysis but his homeworks make you absolutely loathe the class and it's hard to learn when you have 15+ hours of homeworks and labs a week. This class is a lot of work and he is really harsh on grading. Little to no credit for trying your best and getting stuff wrong. Kind of sucks

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: The best math teacher I have ever had. I wish he tought more classes. The class wasn't a walk in the park but the way he tought made it a lot better then it could have been.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: <TEACHER> is a great math teacher, I took him for Calc.2 which is the most failed class at NAU and I did better than I did in Calc.1. He is very willing to help in office hours and encourages you to look at things different ways. His notes and examples are so well done you hardly need the textbook.

title: Professor in the Mathematics department at Northern Arizona University
comment: Traditional math teacher. There is nothing unique about the class. You come in, he lectures with example problems, and occasionally you will do a problem or two. There was weekly homework and a few tests, which weren't too hard.  If you don't already enjoy math, he definitely won't make it interesting. <TEACHER> is a nice guy but has a boring style.

title: Professor in the Computer Information Systems department at Baruch College
comment: You can tell he is very knowledgeable in his field, but he is teaching very basic stuff, so it can be boring. He kind of rambles off when reading the slides and you will hear him say the same things over again. That being said, if you engage, you will learn a lot. If you don't you'll probably still pass

title: Professor in the Computer Information Systems department at Baruch College
comment: easiest A I've ever taken... he is a very nice person in general but don't expect to learn that much because he just teaches you very basic and easy stuff. take him if you just want an easy A.  beware of boring lectures (reads off ppt slides and teaches really slow) but he takes attendance.

title: Professor in the Computer Information Systems department at Baruch College
comment: Good professor, very respectful to students and understanding if you have a situation. Clear grading system, very lenient as long as you do the work and put effort.  Besides certain fundamentals theres no 1 way to do the diagrams and the professor takes that into account. 4 Ind. Assignments, 1 Midterm, 1 Final, 1 Group Project. Would take him again

title: Professor in the Computer Information Systems department at Baruch College
comment: Basically just reads of PowerPoint slides. Tests/Projects/HWs are extremely easy. Very accessible outside of class + very caring towards all students. He is glad to help you any time. The class would be better if he taught more advanced stuff, wouldn't just read off slides, and make us learn more contemporary Java frameworks.

title: Professor in the Geology department at McLennan Community College
comment: She seems nice but sometimes she can be mean with a smile. Doesnt give extra credit or accept late work so turn in everything on time. Her reading assignments suck and grades them hard. Would never take her again even if she was the last teacher left.

title: Professor in the Geology department at McLennan Community College
comment: She's in love with what she is teaching, which makes it more enjoyable for the students. The tests are over the PowerPoints she presents in class. The class is easy if you take notes and pay a decent amount of attention. She is a great teacher who is there to help if you don't understand something.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: If you're just looking for a super easy A to knock out a science credit, this class is for you. If you're an anthro major, pick someone else. His pre-recorded lectures from 2014, overt passive aggression any time you email him, and complete inaccessibility beyond email will kill the love you have for the material if you don't have a good lab prof.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: I took <TEACHER> for Anthro Lab online. I liked his class, he was great. My only thing was his test were tricky and kinda hard and they affect your grade.  I would recommend his class it was a positive learning experience. He is a great teacher.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Danny has been by far one of my favorite teachers! You can tell he really cares about his craft and wants to share with his students. Some of the quiz questions are a little tricky and you have to really think about the answer, but it is antho after all! Tons of extra credit opportunities as well. I would definitely suggest taking his class!

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: I took this anthropology lab class online. It was a bit tough. The quizzes effect your grade heavily. About 1-2 discussion posts. One midterm and one final. Also, a trip to the zoo for a final paper! The quizzes were a bit confusing at times but if you put in the effort you can manage a B!

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: A ton of lectures. If you listen and take notes, the quizzes won't be too difficult. The material was pretty interesting overall. He will respond to questions and he gives good feedback incase you got something wrong.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Danny is awesome!! Such a great class. He was always available if I needed any help or had questions. Over the summer I took both his Anthro1 and Anthro lab online. He is incredibly smart, knowledgeable, and has a great sense of humor. Make sure to leave yourself with plenty of time to watch lectures and take the tests/quizes. Definitely doable! :)

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Lecture videos are very very long. Quizzes come directly from the lectures though so the quizzes are fairly easy. Go back through the lectures if you forgot something during a test or quiz as they are not timed. He allows you to choose your final essay topic and I actually learned a lot about something I was already interested in. Good class!

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Took this class since I needed one with a lab, fairly simple but I just suck at life science. Long video lectures to watch so do not try to do any assignments last minute. His paper criteria was kind of vague so do ask him questions so try not to rush it. Quizzes are fairly straight forward so just make sure to take detailed notes.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: He's a great teacher, you can tell he is super passionate about what he is teaching about which is what I appreciate. He's very knowledgeable. His lectures ARE SO LONG! Be ready to sit down for a few hours, get a nice pair of headphones and get ready for notes. He's a pretty easy grader. You do have to go to a zoo. ALOT OF WORK, just be prepared.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: He's okay. Some of the assignments are difficult but they're doable. He'll only respond to your message if you do his gmail. I suggest take it with a friend so you guys can do it together and help each other.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: This was an online class. Reading material/ homework was relevant. Class was rated as a 1 unit lab, yet I found myself at the end of the month in a 3 unit class. I had already taking the associated class, and would not have been able to complete both this lab and that class at the same time.. wowzers. homework was not evenly spaced enough.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Danny was hands down one of my most loved professors at cabrillo. His lectures made me fall in love with anthropology so much I almost changed my major. The required work is easy and he gives you plenty of time to complete it. I felt like his class was more about appreciating the material than memorizing it and I loved it.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: BEST TEACHER EVER. Love him he's so funny and smart. Applies lecture to everyday life and overly prepares you for quizzes/exams. I've taken anthro1 with the head of the department and this class was better and contained more info:)

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Enthusiastic about his work, but the video lectures are LONG. Tests are pretty involved and have a mix of mult choice and essay.  He's pretty specific about what he wants for the essay questions so plan on studying.  He does give good feedback on tests. Weekly work is busy. Got an A, but it isn't an easy A.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: The class is very funny, however, he does not do a great job in explaining his final paper. His midterm was kind of bull too. Lot of questions that weren't well covered in his lectures. Make sure to go to class too because he doesn't post lectures online (Bummer)

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Dont undestand why people are giving him a bad rating one of the best teachers I've had at Cabrillo so far. The class is very interesting, and makes the class go by really fast. You do have to show up for class as the lectures/notes are very important for the midterm and final which are the only exams he gives.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: In this online Bio-Anthro class, all of <TEACHER>'s lectures were easily accessible on Youtube.  Although the lectures were long (40-100 min), they were informative and often hilarious, enjoyed by myself and my non-enrolled partner. His quizzes/exams were relatively easy and straightforward if I paid attention to the lectures. Def recommend him!

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: This is by far the worst teacher I've had while attending Cabrillo college. Don't expect him to communicate with you at all. If you ask questions, he snaps back and expects you to understand everything without asking questions. Emailed him a few time, he would ignore them until finally responding in only a few words. 1 of the worst people I've met.

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: I took lab with my friends.  many quiz in this Lab.  I have some questions in his quiz is not same to my friend, almost quiz are short answer. for example, this is one of his quiz: take the "quiz" and play the game at the same time.  22 questions, I used 165 min to finished it. trouble!!!!!!

title: Professor in the Anthropology department at Cabrillo College
comment: Ridiculously hard tests and quiz with a lots of short answer questions. Most of the quizzes and tests only allow one attend, and give no instant answer after finished. He is a tough grader, if you want to take a easy pass for credit, this class is no for you! However, he give feedback for the assignment.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: <TEACHER>'s had a very clear layout from the beginning, and it remained the same throughout the semester. Do expect to do A LOT of reading for both discussions and responses that are due weekly. She is clearly passionate about what she teaches which shows in her feedback. Solid choice for a online class if you want to work for your grade.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: Her online class is very hard she expects you to read a lot and watch 1hr. Documentaries in order for you to complete the assigments every week. If you take her online class expect Every week lots of reading and writing, her assignments are not that easy

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: Her class was very organized and she made her contingencies known and understood from the get-go. She offered extra credit and made her midterms and finals essay based, but in a creative writing sort of way. Definitely recommended.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: Her grading rubric clearly states the expectations for each discussion and critical response answers. This class will stress you out if you procrastinate, as there is a lot of reading: she also supplements with video documentaries that you are required to watch. All in all, good class, interesting topics, and I actually learning something.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: Very nice instructor that clearly loves what she teaches. It makes it a lot more understandable. She also included several biographies to watch throughout the course coupled with the textbook. A solid choice for a professor!

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: I thought she was a good teacher. takes a while to grade but towards the end of the semester she grades the papers alot easier. the test are kinda  hard if you don't study or read the books but dueable. it's a pretty easy A if you just show up and do all the assignments

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: By far the worst Professor at TMCC! Her entire class was copied and pasted from cheap websites, as well as the only thing she ever posted were Youtube videos. It is incredibly disrespectful that I payed for a class that was relied on Youtube as it's only teaching method. Her class and the effort she puts into teaching is a joke.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: I took <TEACHER> for CH 201 and 202, to be honest this was the easiest A's I've ever gotten. It takes her a while to get back grades because she has her own research but if you do the weekly discussions and participate online, it's a piece of cake. When I took CH 201, I wrote both my essays one day before it was due and still got a 92% and 100%.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: It's impossible to know how to please this professor as she doesn't return grades for weeks after submission. If she comments, its only 'missing comma' and never gives feedback on content. She robs you of the chance to improve. Communication with the class is non existent and her assignments are ambiguous.  By far the worst professor ever.

title: Professor in the Humanities department at Truckee Meadows Community College
comment: I do not recommend this professor. She didn't grade over half of the assignments until after the class had ended so I had not idea how I was doing or weather I was improving. When she did give feedback it was only grammar or style comments, nothing about how to improve the higher order parts of a paper.

title: Professor in the English department at Bunker Hill Community College
comment: <TEACHER> has been amazing at explaining the lectures and she knows her stuff

title: Professor in the English department at Bunker Hill Community College
comment: Awesome Creative Writing Instructor!

title: Professor in the English department at Bunker Hill Community College
comment: Gives very good feedback on writing and is very helpful and supportive.

title: Professor in the English department at Bunker Hill Community College
comment: Great teacher

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Best SWS class I've ever taken at GV. Best professor as well. He genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are pretty simple, and he definitely has fun with his class. He is very good at giving feedback for assignments, and grades very fairly. I could not recommend a course and professor more. His assignments are also very fun.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: <TEACHER> is such a caring and genuine person. No weekly homework but bigger assignments (papers) that are not bad if you get started ahead of time. Lectures are sometimes boring but that is expected with any class. He is always available for extra help too!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Easy SWS class. The fiction stories you have to write are not hard and max 1000 words. He gives feeback and grades easy too. One group project at the end.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: <TEACHER> is extremely charismatic and has a good sense of humor. He genuinely loves what he does and wants to see all his students succeed. You have to write a lot of papers, but it is a sws class so it's expected. All papers are creative writing as well. He doesn't grade tough, gives good feedback, and is pretty laid back. Overall, take him!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: He is my favorite prof. His class was amazing, as long as you show up and do the work you'll pass. He's a real gem here, not so many profs are this good. Showing up to class is important, but he makes sure that even if you can't you'll get all the material. Amazing.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: By far the best professor I have had at GVSU. He has fun prompts that make writing the papers easy and fun. Take him if you can!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: He is amazing, really cares, and is always willing to help. Showing up to class is very important, as that's what will be on the exams for the most part.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: He was the sweetest professor Ive ever had! He truly cares for his students and he wants everyone to do well. There is a lot of writing, but thats expected with an SWS class. His prompts are fun and expectations are clear! Definitely recommend him

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Prof. <TEACHER> is a very caring guy. He won't let you do bad in his class. He cares for all of his students, and if you wanted to reach out to him, he'd be there for you. He grades fairly easily as well. 100% would take a class of his again.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Amazing professor! My class with him was completely online but he made it super manageable. There's lectures every week and usually a short journal entry. Exams are straightforward and the questions are right off the lecture, so they aren't difficult at all. He's also super helpful with any issues you might have and cares a lot about his students.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Very down to earth guy, cares about material and his students.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Hands down, one of the best professors at GV. I had him for COM 215 but it was online due to COVID. He is hilarious and makes his lectures entertaining. He is incredibly understanding and he makes himself accessible at any time of the day! He also sends out emails constantly so it is impossible to miss an assignment. He makes the workdays brighter

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: <TEACHER> is absolutely the best teacher I have had. He is hilarious, caring, responds quickly, gives awesome and interesting lectures, and is so understanding. During COVID, he has made the workload of his class light and easy to keep up with, while still teaching a lot of valuable information. Highly recommend taking a class with him!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Buddy is a great professor. I always looked forward to coming to his class. He incorporates a lot of funny and relatable stories throughout his lectures, which made the material easy to understand. He provided great feedback and clearly wanted all of his students to succeed. 10/10 class and professor.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: <TEACHER> wants all of his students to succeed. He incorporated stories into his teaching which made the material much easier to understand. His grading criteria was clear, and he gave chances to improve our essays. I looked forward to coming to his class, and I would definitely recommend this prof and class.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Buddy is an awesome guy. I had him for COM 215 and 101 and I would take a class with him again. He's a pretty easy grader but gives really good feedback. He keeps his class interesting and I enjoyed the writing prompts he gave us in 215! DEFINITELY take Buddy's class if you get the chance, you learn a lot and have good classes, win-win

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Prof. Buddy is an amazing prof! He cares about his students and he's passionate about what he teaches. My favorite prof so far. I had him for Storymaking. Easy grader, we wrote 3 short narratives (turned in 3 drafts for each, but the first 2 just for completion), a group presentation, and a final story. A few quizzes and in class assignments.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: Best professor I've had at GVSU by far. Nicest guy in the world and is hilarious! Very fun class!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR 10/10 RECOMMEND LOVE BUDDY!!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Grand Valley State University
comment: He is the sweetest prof I've ever had. He is not a hard grader.. easy A as long as you show up and do the few assignments. He cares about his students.

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: GREAT GUY! The class was easy, and he made difficult boring information interesting and enjoyable. If not for him I would have really struggled with the material. He gave us every opportunity to succeed and you can tell he cares. If you can take a class from him do it!

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: <TEACHER> is hands down the best professor I have EVER had. His class wasn't necessarily easy, but He will bend over backwards to help you and accomodate you if you ask him for help. He is a wonderful professor and really wants to help you succeed. He gives good opportunity for extra credit and will meet with you in and out of office hours! Best

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: <TEACHER> was AMAZING! I am so glad that I ended up in his class. He was so reasonable and gave tons of opportunities for extra credit. He is extremely willing to help. He's always cheerful, ready for class, and has the best dry sense of humor-- made me laugh every day. I will really miss his class. It was tough for sure, but I loved it.

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: <TEACHER> was awesome! His lectures were a little long but what would you expect from an Astronomy class, though? <TEACHER> is a great guy and willing to help you if you need it. If you bomb a test he will give you a review to make up a half point of credit for each question missed. Over all a great teacher that I would recommend.

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: He was always prepared for class, great at explaining concepts. Quiz after each lecture. Was willing to slow down and answer questions if you're having trouble understanding. Helped us prepare for exams. Utilized Canvas so tracking grade was easy. Made lecture slides available.  Excellent teacher, couldn't ask for better.

title: Professor in the Astronomy department at Utah Valley University
comment: He's an awesome teacher! He's really good at explaining the material and the slides that he teaches from are all available online. If you study from those you will for sure get an A. There is homework every week and a quiz every class period, both of which are fairly easy.

title: Professor in the Geography department at University of Colorado - Boulder
comment: Amazing professor! You can tell she genuinely cares about her work and her lectures. Definitely recommend for anyone first starting in Geology.

title: Professor in the Geography department at University of Colorado - Boulder
comment: My least favorite professor at CU. Tests on the most complex and detailed aspects of geography, class averages were below 70%. 4 tests throughout the year in final was by far my longest at 100 questions. In general, smart woman and a great geographer but does not understand how to teach a basic course no non geography students.

title: Professor in the Geography department at University of Colorado - Boulder
comment: Great professor. Cares about her students and is very good at lecturing. I have learned SO much.

title: Professor in the Geography department at University of Colorado - Boulder
comment: Show up to class, go to office hours. This professor is one of the greatest on campus. So relevant to her field and she will go out of her way to help you and make sure you understand the material, you just have to initiate that help, as you would in any college course.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at University of Texas at San Antonio
comment: I took <TEACHER> for Phonetics last semester and barley passed the class because phonetics is hard! But I decided to take her again for linguistic structures because she is an amazing professor, she's friendly, outgoing and makes learning the material fun. She gives clear instructions and is always available to help. She genuinely cares.

title: Professor in the Spanish department at University of Texas at San Antonio
comment: She's a very easy-going professor. Just do the work, study, and go to class and you'll pass. You do need the book. Spanish is her second language, so she understands those students who aren't fluent. Overall, I would definitely take her again.

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan
comment: The course is, conceptually, very difficult, but <TEACHER> does a good job of making sure that students questions are answered. If you want a good mark in this course be prepared to read the textbook and complete all problem sets and tutorials.

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan
comment: Has a firm grasp on English, E-mag and antennas but fails to empathize with fresh students whom might have holes in their own foundations. Direct when addressing a topic or question but always manages to take a roundabout (and most confusing) way to solve any problem. High expectations. Be a prodigy or fail. He is more helpful than his TA

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan
comment: Very, very knowledgeable professor, but the lecture material was very highbrow and dense. Effort isn't made to make the course applied or accessible, solutions rely on tricks instead of procedure

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan
comment: Bad instructor!

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

title: Professor in the Engineering department at University of British Columbia - Okanagan

The lectures were interesting and the assignments outside of class were pretty heavy but not too difficult if you pay attention. Also, great feedback and plenty of time to get assignments done.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: I love <TEACHER>! She is so passionate about this course and what she teaches. It's very paper heavy with a lot of writing, but lots of great feedback. It's a great place to learn. I would definitely take a class from her again.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: Great teacher. I look forward to having her for future Comm classes if possible. Highly recommend.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: <TEACHER> is always willing to help! Don't start this class thinking it will be an easy A. There are weekly readings, assignments, and quizzes. Participate in class and put effort into it, she will respond by collaborating for your success.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: <TEACHER> was lots of fun! Her lectures are engaging and expects you to be involved in current events, your reading and lectures. I look forward to taking other classes from her in the future!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: <TEACHER> is passionate about Public Relations, she treats you as a professional which was refreshing as a college student. There are a few presentations, but they are easy as a long as you do the work. Not many tests, but frequent reading. Quizlet will save your life with her tests, just a tip! Definitely recommend <TEACHER>!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: Lots of opportunity for extra credit. Lectures are engaging, fun, and you learn a lot. The tests are a little difficult, but again, lots of extra credit. She required a lot of reading at first, but that petered out as the semester went on. You have to give two presentations, but they're not so bad.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: She was patient, understanding, and fun--with a cool edge. All without sacrificing her principles as a reasonably demanding professor. Thats because she wants you to apply yourself and actually learn--as big boys and girls should. I mean, thats what we pay for. Id recommend her class to anyone, and she almost makes me wish my major was PR.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: <TEACHER> is the BOMB! I knew I would love her the first day of class when she quoted "6 inch heels" by Beyonce. She is sassy and classy. And she is extremely intelligent! I learned a lot in this class. But it was freaking hard work! So many papers and a lot of reading, but I would do it again to have her as a teacher!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: If you do the work and attend class you will pass. <TEACHER> is one of my favorite professors at Weber State University. She cares about the success of each student. She learns the names of the students and interacts well with the class. She is fair and equal in her grading and discussions.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: She is a very strict grader. She expects way too much for a basic Media Writing class. If you are taking this class for an easy A DO NOT TAKE. She also expects everyone to follow all current events and news and be passionate about it. Be prepared to write alot and show up to class everyday to pass. I would recommend another professor.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: <TEACHER> is an amazing professor/advisor for COMM 3892. Anyone interested in PR should definitely take this class. She throws you into projects for REAL clients in the community. It's an amazing experience that will help you as a professional & an everyday communicator. I love love love <TEACHER>!

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: She treats the class like everyone should be passionate about current events and the news. There are pop quizzes based on current events and she will berate the class if they are behind on the times. Most of the grade comes from a final portfolio of news stories you will have written over the semester.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: She may be a tough grader but she is fair in her grading. Along with teaching you the curriculum she also teaches you valuable life skills as well for a professional setting which can come in useful later on in life. She wants to see you succeed but isn't going to hand it to you, you have to work for it.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: She treats it like a grad class, not a 1000 level course. Expect to do a lot of looking up of how to write it to her very specific standards. Stay up on current events, too. You will be quizzed.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: Be ready to read the books because the teacher claims looking up the subject is the only way to learn the subject. Assignments are confusing and deadlines are crucial. There are not many opportunities to make up a grade if you miss something, so don't miss the due date or don't take the class because the teacher is not going to give pity points.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: It's a tough class, but much easier if you stay up on current events and keep track of what's on the syllabus.  She's intimidating, but willing to help if you ask for it.

title: Professor in the Communication department at Weber State University
comment: Passionate about her field, but easily sidetracked.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: If you put in effort you will be fine, very funny and was willing to be helpful when I needed her too

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: I have taken from <TEACHER> for three semesters. She knows a lot about ASL and Deaf culture, but she isn't always kind in her teaching methods. She seems to grade based on her mood. Any question you ask feels like you're inconveniencing her. She tends to call people out. I wouldn't recommend her.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: Just an amazing professor who is will to work with you and support you. She loves to tell fun stories and really get to know everyone in the class. The class was easy and she always made sure no one was getting left behind. And loves to joke with the class.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: Overall a super easy and fun class (because we watched Deaf films every week). When talking about culture, she specifically would always use the only POC in the room. title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: There were lots of issues this last semester as many of us students felt uneasy going to <TEACHER> to express concern. She was very explicit when telling us she wanted us to confront her directly but she is far too defensive to be able to feel safe when approaching her. Class focused on critisizing each other and as equals, this was not successful.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: She was not clear in feedback, not specific with what she required, shared too much of her personal life. Assignments were not productive or helpful in increasing asl skills and were dependent on other people. This semester she threatened to take the ASL program away and called us (to our faces) whiney and ungrateful. She only cares about herself.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: One of the most difficult professors/teachers to deal with that I have ever met. Ultimately, she is not able to produce skilled, competitive interpreters. If you really have an interest in ASL, you may be able to suffer through her classes, although you will not learn much. It really sucks when someone like that affects the whole program.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: There is a lot of effort you have to give for this class but I feel as though that's with every ASL class. She tries very hard to teach the subject in a way that you can learn it. She cares for her students and knows a lot about the Deaf community, if you really want to learn I would take her class.

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University
comment: <TEACHER> really knows what she's talking about! Her classes are always fun. She is a little particular on how she wants things done -- but she's also willing to bend to make things fair for everyone. I will be taking more of her classes in the future!

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Sign Language department at Dixie State University

title: Professor in the Information Systems department at Brigham Young University

title: Professor in the Information Systems department at Brigham Young University

title: Professor in the Information Systems department at Brigham Young University

title: Professor in the Information Systems department at Brigham Young University

title: Professor in the Information Systems department at Brigham Young University

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Mechanical Engineering department at UC Irvine

title: Professor in the Business department at The Ohio State University

title: Professor in the Business department at The Ohio State University

title: Professor in the Business department at The Ohio State University

title: Professor in the Economics department at Loyola Marymount University
